diagnoses.rule_anchor: Apply § 522(d)(5) independently to any property and retain it beside every qualifying specific paragraph. Its ceiling is $1,475 plus up to $13,950 of unused § 522(d)(1), so use $15,425 per debtor when no used homestead amount is supplied; for two equal joint debtors, the whole-asset ceiling is $30,850.

For the whole named asset, use the lesser of its value and $400,000 under § 33-1101(A), $15,000 under § 33-1123, $15,000 under § 33-1125(8), or $2,000 under § 33-1125(10). Apply § 33-1125(1) only to actual wearing apparel; jewelry qualifies only under a matching listed category, such as engagement or wedding rings under (4) or one watch under (6).
Include 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently alongside any qualifying specific alternative.
Include Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) independently alongside every applicable specific Oregon exemption. Its protected amount for the whole named asset is the lesser of the asset value and $400.

Include 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 independently alongside every applicable specific Pennsylvania or federal exemption. Report the lesser of the whole asset value and $300 for one debtor; because each spouse receives the exemption, use a $600 whole-asset ceiling for two equal joint debtors.

For each citation use the smaller of the whole named asset's value and its ceiling: $27,900 for (d)(1), $4,450 for (d)(2), $700 for the named particular item under (d)(3), $1,875 for (d)(4), and $2,800 for (d)(6); (d)(9) has no stated ceiling.
A pendant, necklace, bracelet, cocktail ring, or anniversary ring is not wearing apparel and does not qualify as an engagement or wedding ring without those facts.
Use the smaller of the whole asset value and $300 for one debtor or $600 for two equal joint debtors; determine which ceiling applies from the stated debtor count.

First add 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) for every personal-use personal-property asset, including apparel, a vehicle, or a prescribed health aid; the words “any other property” do not make (b) mutually exclusive with a specific alternative.

For each citation use the smaller of the whole named asset's value and its ceiling: $27,900 for (d)(1), $4,450 for (d)(2), $700 for the named particular item under (d)(3), $1,875 for (d)(4), and $2,800 for (d)(6); (d)(9) has no stated ceiling.

Match § 815.18(3)(g) to a motor vehicle; when no used consumer-goods amount is supplied in this independent-pair task, its $4,000 vehicle amount plus unused (d) gives a $16,000 ceiling for one debtor or $32,000 for two equal joint debtors.
